about.title: Placerville Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Placerville's mix of Gold Rush-era buildings downtown, busy retail stretches along Placerville Drive and Broadway, and older sidewalks throughout town creates plenty of opportunities for uneven pavement, poor lighting, or spills to go unaddressed. When a property owner or business fails to fix a known hazard or warn visitors about it, California law allows an injured person to seek compensation - but proving what the owner knew and when is often the hardest part of these cases. That's why documentation matters from the very first moment: photos of the hazard, the shoes you were wearing, any witnesses nearby, and a written incident report if the location has one. Surveillance footage at grocery stores, restaurants, and shops along US-50 or Placerville Drive is frequently overwritten within days or weeks, so acting quickly can make a real difference. LawProactive connects Placerville residents and visitors with an independent attorney, free of charge, to help sort through what happened and what comes next.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Placerville Falls

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises law requires showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and enough time to fix or warn about it. An attorney can help gather evidence, like maintenance logs or prior complaints, to build that case.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many Placerville businesses along Broadway and Placerville Drive recycle security footage within days. Getting a preservation request out early can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly distracted or not watching your step, you may still recover a percentage of damages. An attorney can help explain how that math might apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Placerville?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public sidewalk or county building, the deadline to act is much shorter. It's worth having a case reviewed early so no window closes unexpectedly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the fall?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you share some responsibility. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help assess how this might affect your specific case.

items.question: Do I need proof the property owner knew about the hazard?
items.answer: Yes, generally you need to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the dangerous condition and failed to address it. This is often the central issue in premises liability cases. Photos, witness statements, and any available surveillance footage from the location can help establish this.

items.question: Where in Placerville do these incidents tend to happen?
items.answer: Falls are often reported at retail and commercial properties along corridors like Placerville Drive and Broadway Drive, where foot traffic is heaviest. That said, a hazard can occur anywhere property isn't properly maintained, from parking lots to interior walkways.
